# Agentic ODI [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- ## 📋 Table of Contents - [The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation](#-the-vision-context-aware-innovation) - [Current State (Experimental Testbed)](#-current-state-experimental-testbed) - [Code Overview](#-code-overview) - [Getting Started](#-getting-started) - [Command-Line Interface (CLI)](#-command-line-interface-cli) - [Manage Customer Outcomes](#-manage-customer-outcomes) - [External Connectors (MCP Ingest)](#-external-connectors-mcp-ingest) - [One-Command Launch](#-one-command-launch-recommended) - [Manual Split-Terminal](#-manual-split-terminal-alternative) - [Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend](#-local-tools-capable-llm-backend-for-mcp-testing) - [Agent-Driven Testing](#-agent-driven-testing) - [Linting, Formatting & Type Checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) - [Testing](#-testing) - [Test Coverage Map](#-test-coverage-map) - [Agent Session Tracking](#-agent-session-tracking) - [Superpowers with Pi](#-superpowers-with-pi) - [Developer Workflow for Formatting](#-developer-workflow-for-formatting) - [Deployment](#-deployment) - [Roadmap & Next Steps](#-roadmap--next-steps) - [Contributing](#-contributing) - [License](#-license) --- ## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation **Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis. **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes. --- ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed) This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery. --- ## 🧩 Code Overview This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of **six** installable projects, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport). | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | **The Living Studio** — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation. Provides an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous conversational agent connected to the MCP server. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Studio UI together. | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides version/help plus `outcomes` and `connectors` commands. | | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations. The first kind is an **MCP client connector** that connects to a remote MCP server over HTTP, checks health, and ingests tools/resources into a local ingest sink. Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same protocol later. | --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Prerequisites - **Python** 3.10+ - [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling): ```bash uv sync --all-packages ``` This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode. ### 💻 Command-Line Interface (CLI) The [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal — no chat UI required. It provides version and help information plus commands for connecting to external systems. Over time it will also expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes). Launch it with: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # show help when no command is given ``` A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way. ### 🎯 Manage Customer Outcomes Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`): ```bash # Add a Customer Outcome agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" # List outcomes (optionally filtered) agentic-odi outcomes list agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id # Get, update, delete agentic-odi outcomes get agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 agentic-odi outcomes delete --yes # Compute ODI Opportunity Score agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2 ``` Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed. ### 🔌 External Connectors (MCP Ingest) Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). The first kind is `mcp`: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP **client** and pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an external MCP **server**. ```bash python -m cli connectors add mcp --name gong --url http://localhost:9000/mcp --tool latest_quote python -m cli connectors list python -m cli connectors health --name gong python -m cli connectors ingest --name gong ``` Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are not written into the ODI jobs/outcomes store. ### ⚡ One-Command Launch (recommended) `python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Studio UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both. ```bash python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio UI | http://localhost:8501 | ### 🔧 Manual Split-Terminal (alternative) Open two terminals and run each process separately: ```bash # Terminal 1 — MCP server python -m mcp_server # Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI streamlit run client/src/client/app.py ``` ### 🧠 Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend (for MCP testing) To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 1. **Install a local LLM server** Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): ```bash pip install llama-cpp-python ``` 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`): ```bash python -m llama_cpp.server \ --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \ --model_alias local-tools-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \ --chat_format openai ``` This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`. 4. **Configure the Streamlit client** `client/src/client/app.py` reads the following environment variables (with sensible defaults): | Variable | Default | |---|---| | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **"LLM Configuration"**. 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server** - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models ``` If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server. - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above). - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository."* - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together. - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup. ### 🤖 Agent-Driven Testing Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results. --- ## 🧹 Linting, Formatting & Type Checks (CI parity) The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with: ```bash # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml) uv run ruff check . uv run ruff format --check . # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies) uv run --directory core mypy . uv run --directory mcp_server mypy . uv run --directory local_server mypy . uv run --directory client mypy . uv run --directory cli mypy . uv run --directory connectors mypy . # Security scanning uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src # Tests (same as CI) uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` To run these automatically before each commit, enable the bundled pre-commit hooks: ```bash uv tool install pre-commit pre-commit install ``` After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with: ```bash pre-commit run --all-files ``` --- ## ✅ Testing Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact: ```bash uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` ### 📊 Test Coverage Map | File | What it covers | |---|---| | `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation | | `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` jobs/steps/outcomes and Customer Outcome CRUD | | `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool | | `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation | | `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools | | `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` | | `local_server/tests/test_api.py` | Local FastAPI health endpoint | | `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) | | `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior | | `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub | | `cli/tests/test_connectors_cli.py` | CLI `connectors` add/list/health/ingest adapter | | `connectors/tests/test_registry.py` | JSON connector registry persist/load and kind checks | | `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py` | In-memory FastMCP health and ingest records | **Conventions:** - Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`. - Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. - Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests. - The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test. > [!TIP] > Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically. ### 🧪 Agent Session Tracking Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints. --- ## 🤝 Superpowers with Pi This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded. To enable: 1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh` 2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve` 3. Start Pi: `pi` The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi will clone it and load: - **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and after compaction - **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development, systematic-debugging, etc.) > [!NOTE] > Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer. ### 🧼 Developer Workflow for Formatting - **When editing Python files**, either: - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing: ```bash uv run ruff format . ``` - **CI behavior**: - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files. - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only. - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again. --- ## ☁️ Deployment The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents. ### 🧪 Test Chat (UI) Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser: > **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)** ### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint Integrate via the MCP protocol at: > **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)** > [!IMPORTANT] > **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client. --- ## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include: - [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests. - [ ] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: Turn connector records into jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI store. - [ ] **Additional connector kinds**: REST/webhooks and similar integrations implementing the same `Connector` protocol. - [ ] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*, *Steps*, and *Outcomes*. - [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `cli/` so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path. - [ ] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like `get_job_map(job_id)` or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`. - [ ] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the fastmcp server to a lightweight vector or relational database containing actual user research data. - [ ] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the client up to an LLM (e.g., via LangChain or standard OpenAI clients) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features. --- ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Please ensure any change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) before opening a pull request. --- ## 📄 License No license has been specified for this repository yet. # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails

This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.

> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `knowledge/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.

---

## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails

This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.

### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?

ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.

ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.

---

### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done

- A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
- A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
- **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
- ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.

---

### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes

- **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
- Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
- **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):

  > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`

  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.

- **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.

---

### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)

- All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
  1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
  2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
  3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
  4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
  5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
  6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
  7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
  8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs

- **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
- ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.

# First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Design

**Date:** 2026-10-16
**Status:** Draft for builder check
**Scope:** CLI first-launch experience + persistent PM baseline profile

## Intent & Why

Agentic ODI ships 69 PM skills (vendored from Paweł Huryn's pm-skills) and an ODI/JTBD agent, but nothing establishes *who the user is* — domain, audience, business model, current goal. Every skill run starts cold, asking generic questions or guessing. The fix: one designed first-run moment that captures (mostly auto-detects) a minimal product/domain baseline, persists it, and lets the agent and skills consume it forever after.

Jobsian bar: the PM should never fill out a form. They give **one input — a product URL or company name** — the CLI fetches and infers, prints a small confirmation card, and one keypress completes setup. Typed questions exist only as fallback when the fetch fails or inference is unclear. Total happy-path effort: ~30 seconds, one keystroke.

## Goals

- First `agentic-odi` invocation (interactive TTY) triggers a short, designed onboarding moment instead of a bare help screen.
- Happy path: **URL → fetch → infer → confirm card → done**.
- Fallback path (fetch fails / non-obvious site / user prefers typing): **3 typed questions with suggested defaults**.
- Baseline persisted to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (XDG-overridable); never re-prompts once the file exists.
- `odi setup` re-runs onboarding; `odi profile` shows the current baseline.
- PM skills / agent can later read the baseline file as standing context; follow-ups happen only when a specific task needs missing fields (out of scope to implement here beyond exposing the file and a `profile` command).

## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals

- No long diagnostic questionnaire (the 15-question PM audit is explicitly rejected).
- No LLM call during onboarding (no API key exists yet at first run; inference must be deterministic, offline-capable keyword mapping).
- No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
- No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
- No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).

## User Flow

### 1. Trigger

- Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
- Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
- Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.

### 2. Opening (the designed moment)

```
Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.

Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
First: what product are you working on?
Paste a product URL or company name:
```

### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect

1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
5. Show the confirmation card:

```
Based on sentry.io — does this look right?

  Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
  Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
  Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
  Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging

  [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
```

6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).

### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)

Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):

1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).

Then the same confirmation card and save.

# First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Design

**Date:** 2026-10-16
**Status:** Draft for builder check
**Scope:** CLI first-launch experience + persistent PM baseline profile

## Intent & Why

Agentic ODI ships 69 PM skills (vendored from Paweł Huryn's pm-skills) and an ODI/JTBD agent, but nothing establishes *who the user is* — domain, audience, business model, current goal. Every skill run starts cold, asking generic questions or guessing. The fix: one designed first-run moment that captures (mostly auto-detects) a minimal product/domain baseline, persists it, and lets the agent and skills consume it forever after.

Jobsian bar: the PM should never fill out a form. They give **one input — a product URL or company name** — the CLI fetches and infers, prints a small confirmation card, and one keypress completes setup. Typed questions exist only as fallback when the fetch fails or inference is unclear. Total happy-path effort: ~30 seconds, one keystroke.

## Goals

- First `agentic-odi` invocation (interactive TTY) triggers a short, designed onboarding moment instead of a bare help screen.
- Happy path: **URL → fetch → infer → confirm card → done**.
- Fallback path (fetch fails / non-obvious site / user prefers typing): **3 typed questions with suggested defaults**.
- Baseline persisted to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (XDG-overridable); never re-prompts once the file exists.
- `odi setup` re-runs onboarding; `odi profile` shows the current baseline.
- PM skills / agent can later read the baseline file as standing context; follow-ups happen only when a specific task needs missing fields (out of scope to implement here beyond exposing the file and a `profile` command).

## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals

- No long diagnostic questionnaire (the 15-question PM audit is explicitly rejected).
- No LLM call during onboarding (no API key exists yet at first run; inference must be deterministic, offline-capable keyword mapping).
- No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
- No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
- No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).

## User Flow

### 1. Trigger

- Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
- Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
- Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.

### 2. Opening (the designed moment)

```
Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.

Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
First: what product are you working on?
Paste a product URL or company name:
```

### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect

1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
5. Show the confirmation card:

```
Based on sentry.io — does this look right?

  Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
  Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
  Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
  Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging

  [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
```

6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).

### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)

Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):

1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).

Then the same confirmation card and save.

### 5. After onboarding

## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails

### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
- **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
- **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
  - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
  - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
- **Tool Creation**: 
  - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
  - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
  - **Capability Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update the `get_capabilities` tool's human-readable return string to ensure the capability set exactly matches the code.

### 2. Async / Client Practices
- Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
- Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.

### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
- Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
- When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.

### 4. General Philosophy
- **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
- **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `connectors/` workspace package. New kinds implement `connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
- **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
- **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `connectors/src/connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
- **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
- **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
- **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
- **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.
